posts.name: jagarciao
posts.cooked:
I do believe the difference lies in "regain" vs "restore to". The first (regain) simply says to add a specific amount of hit points to a target... this amount is in turn modifiable by any healing effects that are in play. The only implication with "regain" is that you cannot go past your starting HP (that's why it says REgain and not just simply gain"

The second (restore to) implies that you add whatever amount of HP is necessary to get you to the target amount, so if there are healing effects on play those would be considered while calculating the amount necessary to get you to the target HP. For example, if Fanatic is at -6 HP and there is a +1 to healing then you would add 15HP to get her to 10, but if Fanatic was at -4 and a -2 healing effect was in place then you would add 16 HP to get her to 10. The amount being "healed" or added is affected by the healing modifiers, but the end result is the amount she is being restored to, which is 10. 

That's the way I interpret it.

Recovery should encompass restoring and regaining, and the word all doesn't leave room for exemption, just like Scholar's wording wouldn't cover a restoration of hp, because the wording matches a specific action.

I'm honestly not trying to keep the argument going, I am happy it is on the list of unresolved questions, just wanted to clarify.
